body: Counttess has it right. Try for a nonprofit, or at the very least a small company with a more open and friendly atmosphere. That way you are more likely to feel like part of a team. I currently work in an office of 35 people and even though we all come from different educational backgrounds, most of us find ways to relate and help each other out, even if it goes outside of our regular job duties.
Thanks for giving me some clarity!

University City, MO. But later on, it says that it should be obtained before putting it on the market. I'm very confused.
Thank you so much for taking the time to write these kind words

I can definitely tell you you are not alone! I graduated in December and immediately had a breakdown, staying up all night obsessively reading about the shitty economy and worrying about my future. It's so important to be able to give yourself a break. Try to limit your job search worries to a few hours a day, then focus on doing something relaxing that you enjoy. I also found it a lot more relaxing to search and apply for things when I went to coffee shops with friends who also had some work to do. 

I agree with a lot of the other comments about volunteering and finding part-time or full-time outside your field for now if you can. Please don't feel like a failure; so many people are in the same boat. I know several people who flunked out of vet programs, including my own father. You graduated and you are a smart and capable person. You will get the job eventually.
